overview: Eswatini has effectively no femtech startup scene. Women's health here is dominated by the world's highest HIV prevalence among women and one of the highest cervical cancer burdens on earth, so the real activity sits in public health and donor programming: HIV testing, PMTCT and a growing menu of PrEP options, HPV vaccination and screening, maternal care, and adolescent sexual and reproductive health. Digital health is emerging through government and World Bank systems rather than private ventures, and women-in-tech activity is nascent and largely folded into broader regional programmes.

sections.heading: Latest major news
sections.narrative: Recent milestones cluster around new HIV prevention options, HPV vaccination and maternal mortality gains, amid pressure from global aid cuts.

items.text: The long-acting injectable PrEP cabotegravir (CAB-LA) launches in Eswatini via the Family Life Association of Eswatini, offering women an every-eight-weeks alternative to daily pills amid deep budget cuts.
A second round of the integrated school-based HPV campaign lifts coverage to 69.7% of the targeted 80,000 girls, later expanding routine vaccination to nine-year-olds.
Human Rights Watch urges Eswatini to strengthen enforcement against violence toward women, noting persistent gaps despite the 2018 Sexual Offences and Domestic Violence Act.

sections.heading: Policy & strategy
sections.narrative: Government and partners frame women's health through HIV prevention, cervical cancer elimination, family planning and gender policy.

items.text: The Cervical Cancer Elimination Acceleration Plan 2025-2030 sets national targets for HPV vaccination, screening and treatment against the country's very high cervical cancer burden.
The Ministry of Health and UNFPA launch the 3rd edition of the National Family Planning Guidelines to improve service quality and cut unmet need.
Eswatini launches its National Gender Policy and a National Strategy on Ending Violence (2023-2027), covering health, education and employment.
The NERCHA HIV Prevention 2025 Road Map prioritises adolescent girls and young women and scale-up of ARV-based prevention including PrEP.

sections.heading: Latest ecosystem moves
sections.narrative: Momentum is in public-health delivery and government digital-health systems rather than private femtech.

items.text: The Ministry of Health, with World Bank support, digitises community health services through the electronic Community-Based Health Information System (CBHIS), running offline on handheld devices used by Rural Health Motivators.
Digital handheld devices help Rural Health Motivators close immunisation gaps and reach women and children in remote areas.
MTN Eswatini and the Ministry of ICT roll out digital platforms including the TruMD health service, part of a public-private push into digital service delivery.
UNICEF supports a social-accountability mobile platform for youth-friendly SRH services; in 2024 alone 1,744 young clients submitted 2,875 recommendations.
A dapivirine vaginal ring (PrEP ring) study reports early user and provider experiences as Eswatini expands the menu of women-controlled HIV prevention methods.

sections.heading: Key players & programmes
sections.narrative: The landscape is almost entirely government, UN agencies, NGOs and research programmes; there are no notable local femtech startups.

items.name: Family Life Association of Eswatini (FLAS)
items.note: IPPF member delivering SRH, family planning and PrEP including the new injectable CAB-LA through static clinics

items.name: UNFPA Eswatini
items.note: Leads family planning, maternal mortality reduction and gender-based violence programming under its country programme

items.name: NERCHA (National Emergency Response Council on HIV/AIDS)
items.note: Coordinates the national HIV response and the HIV Prevention 2025 Road Map

items.name: Ministry of Health, Eswatini
items.note: Runs PMTCT, HPV vaccination, cervical cancer screening and the CBHIS digital rollout

items.name: MOSAIC project (USAID/PEPFAR)
items.note: Supports national scale-up of PrEP choice for women, including CAB-LA situation analysis and readiness

items.name: UNICEF Eswatini
items.note: Supports youth-friendly SRH services and a social-accountability mobile feedback platform

items.name: Georgetown Lombardi global cancer researchers
items.note: Partner on cervical cancer screening and prevention research in Eswatini

sections.heading: Notable funding
sections.narrative: There is no femtech venture funding; money flows as donor grants for HIV and vaccine programmes.
